subject: Request: custom uptime annex, latency tiers, and order-form language for LiftBridge
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan.park@liftbridgehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Torres <maria.torres@liftbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA annex request and evidence for order form

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is confident Redwood meets our perf profile. Procurement asked me to consolidate the asks we need to close the PO and internal legal review. High-level:

- We need a short SLA annex (attached) that commits to 99.95% monthly availability for the hosted endpoint used by LiftBridge, with a 95th/99th latency tier for 512-token requests.
- Because some traffic will route to dedicated pools and some to burst-hosted, we want language that clarifies which capacity tier the SLA covers and how cross-tier failover is treated.
- LiftBridge requires evidence: recent SOC2 summary, a traffic matrix (sent separately), and a short ops runbook excerpt describing incident notification windows.
- Procurement also wants any proposed order-form wording for the purchase order and suggested credits table for downtime.

Attached is our basic annex template. Can you confirm Redwood can sign this or provide redline language for the order form? Also, can you indicate what evidence you can share (SOC2 + uptime graphs + incident runbook snippet)?

We'd like to get legal-approved language by next Wednesday (10/27) to meet our vendor onboarding deadlines.

Thanks,
Evan Park
Senior Procurement Manager
LiftBridge Health

Attachment: liftbridge-sla-annex-template.docx (attachment stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@liftbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Maria Torres <maria.torres@liftbridgehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA annex request and evidence for order form

Hi Evan — thanks, and great to hear the demo went well. Looping in Karthik (Contracts) and Irene (Security/Product Ops) so we can align on order-form language and the evidence package.

Short answers up front:
- We can provision a LiftBridge-dedicated pool and commit to availability for requests routed to that pool. For hybrid deployments (dedicated + hosted burst), we can offer a blended SLA model — coverage for dedicated pool traffic with a defined fallback behavior for burst routing.
- We propose a two-tier latency table: P50/P95/P99 for 128-token and 512-token windows. We will include explicit measurement windows and the measurement method (edge-aggregated request logs).
- Evidence: we can share a SOC 2 summary, 90-day uptime/latency graphs for the proposed endpoint, and an extract of our incident notification runbook (redacted where necessary).

Next steps we propose:
1) We will send a redline to your annex and a suggested order-form snippet for the PO (expected by 10/21 EOD).
2) Irene will prepare the security evidence bundle (SOC2 summary + redacted runbook + ops graphs) and share via the Drive link.
3) Karthik will propose specific credit calculations for a 99.95% monthly SLA vs a 99.9% baseline for burst traffic.

Can you confirm the LiftBridge procurement team is comfortable with blended coverage (dedicated pool guaranteed; burst capacity best-effort with reduced credit eligibility)? If not, let us know the absolute requirement for coverage across both modes.

Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_Request_Form.xlsx (internal ref)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@liftbridgehealth.com>, Maria Torres <maria.torres@liftbridgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA annex request and evidence for order form

FW: internal notes -> proposed redline and credit table (see below)

Ava/Irene — drafting notes for the redline I will push to Evan:
- Offer: 99.95% monthly availability for traffic served from the dedicated LiftBridge pool.
- For traffic served from Hosted/Burst capacity: offer a 99.90% soft SLA; credits apply at 99.90% - 99.50% band at 5% of monthly fees per 0.1% below; 99.5% and below escalate to case-by-case remediation; dedicated pool breaches follow the primary credit table.
- Cross-tier failover: explicit exclusion for degradation due to customer-initiated scaling events or third-party cloud interruptions; we will include fallback notification timelines and automatic routing documentation in the runbook excerpt.
- Measurement: availability measured at the HTTP 200 success rate per calendar month, aggregated at the endpoint front-door; latency measured at edge egress in ms per percentile.

Attachments I'll include in the redline package: SLA_Addendum_Draft_LiftBridge_20271020.docx, LiftBridge_Traffic_Matrix_Q3_2027.xlsx, and a simple credits table embed.

Question for Irene: can we include the SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary-2027.pdf) and send uptime graphs aggregated by region? Evan requested a 90-day view; I can produce the credits projections once we confirm the blended model.

-Karthik
Director, Contracts & GTM Legal
Redwood Inference

> On Wed, Oct 20, 2027 at 11:04 AM Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com> wrote:
> > (see above)

From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@liftbridgehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@liftbridgehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA annex request and evidence for order form

Ava/Karthik/Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from LiftBridge legal/procurement:

- Blended coverage is acceptable, but LiftBridge requires a clear clause that documented failover to hosted/burst counts toward SLA measurement for the month only if the failover was initiated by Redwood due to capacity constraints. If the failover was initiated due to customer configuration or scheduled maintenance, it must be excluded.
- We need explicit notification windows: initial incident notification within 15 minutes of detection for Sev1, and a status update every 60 minutes until remediation.
- The credits table needs a hard floor (maximum credit per month capped at 50% of monthly recurring fees).

We're attaching one internal procurement note and a slightly edited annex (see attachment). Can you incorporate these points into your redline and share the redline + evidence bundle by Monday 10/25 EOD? We need final PO language to route to finance.

Thanks,
Maria Torres
Senior Counsel, LiftBridge Health

Attachment: LB_procurement_note_20271022.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@liftbridgehealth.com>, Evan Park <evan.park@liftbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Oct 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA annex request and evidence for order form

Team — delivering the redline and evidence per the timeline. Summary of what is attached to this thread:

1) SLA_Addendum_Draft_LiftBridge_20271020.docx — our redline that: (a) makes the dedicated-pool coverage explicit; (b) adds Redwood-initiated failover inclusion language; (c) includes the notification windows you requested; (d) caps monthly credits at 50% of MRR.
2) LiftBridge_Traffic_Matrix_Q3_2027.xlsx — your traffic matrix backfilled into our capacity planning view (ops ask: confirm burst % assumptions).
3) redwood-soc2-summary-2027.pdf — SOC2 summary with control families and third-party attestations (redacted).
4) Runbook_incident-notification_excerpt.pdf (redacted ops excerpt).
5) OrderForm_PO_Snippet.txt — suggested PO clause with the credits table illustration and a DocuSign template link.

DocuSign link for the order-form + annex (for your legal to review before signature): https://www.docusign.com/templates/LB-uptime-2027-xx
Drive evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1q2w3e4rSLA-evidence

If this looks good, Karthik will finalize credit calculations and Monica (Finance) will align on billing/proration for the first month. If LiftBridge needs any additional evidence, Irene can pull more granular region-by-region latency graphs.

Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
